title: Balancing the Experts: Unlocking LoRA-MoE for GRPO via Mechanism-Aware Rewards
claim: The standard pipeline ignores internal model mechanics; ours adds a module that turns internal routing statistics into a reward signal.
layout: 2 stacked panels split by dashed line, left-to-right flow, new modules highlighted orange
description: Two horizontal flow diagrams are stacked and separated by a dashed line. The top panel, labeled GRPO, runs left to right: a query q goes into a yellow LLM box, which produces a gray column of outputs o1…oG. The outputs feed blue Reference Model and Reward Model boxes. These produce a gray column of rewards r1…rG, then a Group Computation box, then a gray column of advantages A1…AG. Long curved arrows return from the advantages to the LLM. The bottom panel, RO-GRPO, repeats the same layout. The LLM is replaced by 'LLM with LoRA-MoE', and two new orange boxes are added: a Routing Info Aggregator below the LLM and a Routing Reward Function below the Reward Model. The aggregator's output goes to the reward function, which feeds into the rewards column. The orange boxes are the only change and draw the eye first.
caption: Comparison of standard GRPO and our RO-GRPO.
abstract: Parameter-efficient Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, such as LoRA-MoE, enable strong and generalizable fine-tuning. However, a critical problem arises when fine-tuning these architectures with advanced reinforcement learning algorithms such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Traditional supervised techniques are not naturally compatible with the GRPO objective, and naive combinations fail to effectively address routing collapse and the underutilization of MoE adapter parameters. To resolve this disconnect, we introduce Routing-Optimized Group Relative Policy Optimization (RO-GRPO), a mechanism-aware framework. It turns internal expert routing statistics collected during training into a direct reward signal, seamlessly integrating routing supervision into the reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) process. This enables effective optimization of parameter utilization and improves performance on both unimodal and multimodal mathematical reasoning tasks, all without extra training stages. Our work provides the first demonstration that a scalar reward in GRPO can be engineered from a model's own internal mechanics to explicitly guide its optimization, extending alignment from mere behavior tuning to holistic mechanism alignment.
